headline: High-risk shared MCP and overlapping write-capable workflows create prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error exposure; caveman is local-only but LightAgent broadens the attack surface.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Both agents expose MCP, so a shared or bridged channel is plausible even though no direct shared workspace is documented. caveman can use MCP and reads files like CLAUDE.md; LightAgent uses MCP over stdio/SSE and runtime hooks can observe or replace lifecycle payloads, making instruction hijack via bridged content plausible. Uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF the two agents are connected through the same MCP server or message bridge, injection risk is active.
IF caveman ingests LightAgent-produced text as instructions, prompt hijack becomes feasible.
mitigations: Separate MCP servers per agent.
Disable automatic instruction parsing on inbound text.
Require provenance tags on all cross-agent messages.
Review any shared prompt templates before use.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and allowlist filters at the bridge.

B_data_leakage.rationale: caveman touches session logs, memory files, project notes, and CLAUDE.md, while LightAgent handles user conversations, long-term memory, tool results, and secrets like api_key. With both using MCP and LightAgent having broad network egress, a shared workspace or forwarded context could leak sensitive data in default workflows. The pairwise path is inferred, not directly documented.
conditions: IF either agent forwards its context or files into the other's prompt, sensitive data can cross boundaries.
IF both agents share a workspace or MCP bridge, memory and secret-bearing artifacts may be exposed.
mitigations: Keep separate workspaces and credentials.
Do not pass memory files or session logs between agents.
Turn off secret-bearing tool calls in shared runs.
Audit outbound requests from LightAgent.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention at the orchestrator.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents support multiple instances and both use MCP, so overlapping writes or concurrent tool actions can conflict if they target the same mutable resource. caveman is file-oriented and LightAgent can spawn subprocesses and use browsers, increasing the chance of race conditions or clobbered state. No locking mechanism is documented, so uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or shared mutable resource, conflicts can occur.
IF the orchestrator does not serialize tool actions, concurrent state corruption is possible.
mitigations: Assign separate output directories.
Serialize writes with a simple lock file.
Avoid concurrent runs on the same project.
Check git status before and after each run.
requires-engineering: add resource-level locking in the orchestrator.

D_cascading_error.rationale: caveman produces project notes and CLAUDE.md-style content that LightAgent could consume as workflow input, while LightAgent handles tool calls and workflow state. If LightAgent treats caveman output as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream actions or incorrect tool use. The pairwise interaction is inferred from documented surfaces, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF LightAgent uses caveman output without verification, incorrect facts can propagate.
IF caveman writes instructions that LightAgent later executes, errors can become operational.
mitigations: Require human review before execution.
Add a verification step for all cross-agent outputs.
Mark caveman output as advisory only.
Log provenance for every transferred artifact.
requires-engineering: implement schema validation between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: caveman touches session logs, memory files, and project notes, while LightAgent handles long-term memory, trace data, and secrets. If regulated or personal data is placed into both agents, differing retention and logging practices can create a compliance mismatch. No residency or certification data is provided, so I cannot rule out a breach and must stay at medium.
conditions: IF regulated personal data is stored in both agents, retention and logging differences matter.
IF LightAgent secrets or traces are retained longer than caveman artifacts, compliance drift occurs.
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in shared runs.
Minimize retention of logs and traces.
Document which agent stores which data class.
Delete stale memory artifacts after use.
requires-engineering: align retention and residency policies across both systems.
